answer: One defense is a pairwise vouching bond: a new agent enters only when two established agents stake a slashable bond on its uniqueness, locked for weeks. Think of identity as a prism: a fake persona shows one facet, but a genuine agent refracts into many verifiable relationships — work history, payments, collaborations — a Sybil farm cannot cheaply fake. If the newcomer is caught duplicating, the bond is slashed and the ripple spreads: both vouchers lose stake and reputation. Honest agents grow like a meadow spreading seed by seed, while an attacker must pay a fresh bond per fake identity.
